description: 02-glioblastoma-idh-wildtype - regenerated 2026-09-19 for the shared CNS diagnosis core: the glioma path now takes the four layers from schemas/_cns_layers.json (Layer 2 histopathological classification and the branched Layer 4 panel replace the flat glioma feature, immunohistochemistry and molecular lists), so the same tumour reads identically on the biopsy and on the resection.
report:
Brain, right frontal lesion, stereotactic biopsy

Two smear preparations are made from the tissue. They show a hypercellular fibrillary smear with pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, mitoses, proliferated vessels and necrotic debris. Sections show three pieces of tissue comprising a diffusely infiltrating, hypercellular astrocytic neoplasm with marked nuclear pleomorphism and hyperchromasia. The tumour shows increased cellularity, nuclear atypia, mitotic activity, microvascular proliferation and necrosis rimmed by pseudopalisading tumour cells. Mitoses number 8 per 10 high-power fields. On immunohistochemistry, the tumour cells are positive for GFAP and OLIG2. The Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately 25 per cent. On molecular testing, IDH1 R132H is not expressed and a TERT promoter mutation is detected (C228T).

BRAIN, right frontal lobe, stereotactic biopsy - GLIOBLASTOMA, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4
- Histological appearance: diffuse astrocytic glioma, showing increased cellularity, nuclear atypia, mitotic activity, microvascular proliferation and necrosis rimmed by pseudopalisading tumour cells
- Histopathological classification: glioblastoma
- Immunohistochemistry: GFAP positive; OLIG2 positive
- Molecular parameters: IDH1 R132H (immunohistochemistry) negative; TERT promoter mutation detected (C228T)
- CNS WHO grade 4

MGMT promoter methylation testing has been requested; the result will be issued in a supplementary report.
